fine_trace.note: Unconstrained templated constructor takes T1 by value. When instantiated with a Coverage lvalue it makes an unintended stack copy of the whole Coverage object instead of preserving reference semantics.

GSUB closure reached via hb_subset -> hb_ot_layout_lookups_substitute_closure. 'this+coverage' is a const Coverage& (OffsetTo::operator+ returns a reference), so the argument is copied by value into the constructor parameter t1.

fine_trace.code: inline void init (const struct CoverageFormat1 &c_) { c = &c_; i = 0; };
fine_trace.note: The iterator stores a pointer into the constructor's local copy (c_ binds to the dead by-value parameter t1). Once the hb_auto_t constructor returns, that copy is destroyed and c dangles.

fine_trace.code: inline bool more (void) { return i < c->glyphArray.len; }
fine_trace.note: iter.more() dereferences the dangling pointer c and reads c->glyphArray.len from storage that has already been released (use-after-free).

via: by-value copy of Coverage into constructor parameter

vuln_logic.issue_alignment: The unconstrained hb_auto_t constructor copies a Coverage value instead of keeping pointer/reference semantics; Coverage::Iter keeps a pointer into the released copy, so later operations (iter.more/iter.get_glyph) access storage that has already been released. Triggered during GSUB closure (hb_subset -> hb_ot_layout_lookups_substitute_closure -> ReverseChainSingleSubstFormat1::closure).
